[ANND_Right_to_Water_in_Qatar.txt p.14] Qatari law safeguards farmers’ rights to continue withdrawing groundwater free of charge. However, law no. 23 of 2025 places strict rules and regulations on the use of
groundwater and imposes severe penalties for violations.9 For example, all wells must be licensed (Article 10) and have a maximum permitted withdrawal rate (Article 7.2). Furthermore, each well has a permitted area that it may irrigate (Article 13), which cannot be increased without a license. Additionally, wells must be at least 300 meters apart to mitigate over-abstraction (Article 11).
The new law significantly increased penalties for violations. The most severe penalties were reserved for actions that pollute natural water resources, which can reach up to 15 years in prison and a million Qatari riyals in fines (Article 76). Digging an unlicensed well or exceeding the permitted withdrawal rate in a licensed well (without prior permission) is punishable by up to three years in prison and up to 500,000 Qatari riyals in fines (Article 77). Meanwhile, exceeding the licensed irrigated area carries no prison sentence but is punishable by a hefty fine of up to

[QEERI_2022_Qatar_Groundwater_Challenges.txt p.1] So how can groundwater in Qatar be sustainably managed? Kahramaa is actively rehabilitating and activating over 300 existing recharge wells around Qatar, to increase the direct recharge to the aquifer system in the country from the rain and subsequently improve the groundwater condition and increase its availability for water security, while at the same time extending efforts to drill and develop about 60 recharge/injection and observation wells to increase the direct recharge to storage zone and to increase the productivity of the aquifer system from the rain. Managed aquifer recharge (MAR) is not easy or straightforward in Qatar due to the karstic nature of the sub-surface, but Kahramaa’s Water Projects Department budgeted 2.6 billion QAR for projects in 2019 to improve the groundwater storage zones and increase the recharge to the groundwater water aquifer system.
An even more serious issue than the decrease in quality of the groundwater is the issue of land subsidence due to the changes in the water table. For a very flat and low-lying country like Qatar, land changes can actually influence shifts along the coastline of Qatar, exacerbating any issues of sea level rise by changing the level of the land also. Research such as that ongoing at Qatar Environment and Energy Research Institute ( QEERI ), part of Hamad Bin Khalifa University, a member of Qatar Foundation (QF), can help. QEERI’s Earth Science Program partnered with NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in the OASIS project, which intends to use satellites to help map groundwater, land subsidence and sea level changes in this region and beyond. At the same time, QEERI is developing better options for agricultural water and brine management, which can help to protect the groundwater and the environment. Research to allow more crops to be grown with less water, and better greenhouse or other cooler environment options for indoor farming can extend the growing season and reduce the burden on the groundwater system.

answers.question: How many groundwater wells are there in Qatar?
answers.answer:
The number of groundwater wells in Qatar is not explicitly stated in the provided sources. However, it is mentioned that there are 4,564 wells on farms (working and not working) in 2023 [number-of-farms-and-wells-by-type-of-the-farm-and-municipality.csv row 91]. This figure may include both working and non-working wells, and it does not specifically refer to all groundwater wells in the country [general knowledge]. Therefore, the exact number of groundwater wells in Qatar remains unspecified in the given information [general knowledge].

Note on sources: The farm census table counts 4564 wells on farms in 2023 [number-of-farms-and-wells-by-type-of-the-farm-and-municipality.csv row 91], while kahramaa officials have cited more than 6500 agricultural wells (Gulf Times interview, not yet in AquaMaa's database). The sources count differently; the census counts wells on registered farms, working or not.

[NPC_Water_Statistics_2023.txt p.29] 3. Water Resources
3-1 Rationale
Qatar’s only natural freshwater resources are rainfall and groundwater. The
conservation of the quality and quantity of the country’s groundwater resources is one
of the targets of Qatar’s National Development Strategy.
Table 3.1 shows the long-term natural water balance (1998-2023) of Qatar's
groundwater basins. The safe yield of groundwater amounted to 49.6 million m3 per
year. The rate of groundwater withdrawal during the period (1998-2022) was about
250 million m3 per year, causing the depletion of aquifers, low groundwater levels and
increased salinity. In 2023, groundwater abstraction amounted to about 180 million
m3 per year, with the abstracted volume changing due to the Regional Groundwater
Modeling Project in Qatar (Kahramaa Project).
Several projects are also in place to raise the rate of artificial recharge of groundwater
basins (e.g. through recharge wells) and the artificial injection of treated wastewater
and distilled water. The return of irrigation water plays an important role in the overall
water balance.

answers.question: where is the most number of wells in qatar
answers.why: Website 9 Nov: router turned "where" into a count by area; one search with a 2022 filter; gave up and cited a page for the absence
answers.answer:
The municipality with the most number of wells in Qatar is Al Khor, with 1,621 wells in 2023 [number-of-farms-and-wells-by-type-of-the-farm-and-municipality.csv p.249].

The sources count differently; the census counts wells on registered farms, working or not.
